title: No module claimed the request: user not found, or no usable password
plain_english: FreeRADIUS runs the authorize section to find out who the user is and how to check them. No module set Auth-Type, so there was nothing to authenticate with and the reject is automatic. Almost always this means no backend found the user, or a backend found the user but returned no password FreeRADIUS can use with this authentication method.

causes.cause: No backend found the user. The identity often carries a realm or domain prefix (user@corp.example.com, CORP\\user) that the lookup filter does not expect.
causes.next_check: Read the module results above this line ('[ldap] = notfound', 'SQL query returned no results', '[files] = noop'); compare User-Name with Stripped-User-Name and adjust realm stripping (suffix/ntdomain) or the lookup filter.

causes.cause: The user was found but the password is stored in a form this auth method cannot use: MSCHAP needs a cleartext or NT-hash password, and pap will not set Auth-Type without a 'known good' password.
causes.next_check: Look for 'No "known good" password' or 'No NT-Password' in the same request; then check which password attribute the backend actually returns.

causes.cause: The request landed in a virtual server whose authorize section does not list the backend module at all.
causes.next_check: Find the 'Virtual server ... received request' line and check that server's authorize section in sites-enabled/ lists ldap, sql, or files as needed.
